statement: The Rumsey detail page for Coronelli's 1693 'Terre Polari, Artiche, ed Antartiche' returned an access check and its metadata could not be transcribed.
why_it_matters: Act III's central object is unseen. Nothing may be said about what Coronelli's polar plate depicts until the plate itself is examined.
next_action: Retrieve the Rumsey record by hand or find a second digitised copy, then transcribe title, list number, date and rights.

statement: Search evidence suggests the 1693 polar plate is weighted towards the Arctic, and a separate 'Terre Artiche' plate exists.
why_it_matters: If Coronelli's polar plate is mostly northern, the honest Act III finding is that the southern polar region is comparatively unattended, which is a stronger argument than the one the specification assumes.
next_action: Establish whether the Epitome carries a distinct southern polar plate, or whether the south appears only on the globe gores and world maps.

statement: Milanesi's Coronelli monograph has not been consulted.
why_it_matters: Without it Act III would read Coronelli's plates as statements of his beliefs, which is the exact error the claim ledger flags as high risk.
next_action: Acquire or consult the Brepols volume and record page locators for Coronelli's working method and source use.

statement: No specific Atlante Veneto volume or plate has been identified as carrying polar material.
why_it_matters: A thirteen-volume work cannot be cited as a whole. The object register currently holds a placeholder.
next_action: Work through a digitised Atlante Veneto set and list the plates that show the southern polar region.

statement: Both verified Greenwich objects state no reuse licence; the 1910 ice chart carries a Crown copyright credit line.
why_it_matters: The two objects the essay most wants to reproduce are the two whose terms are unknown. Both are research_only until RMG Images answers in writing.
next_action: Write to RMG Images with the intended use, and record the reply against both object rows.

statement: Greenwich holds at least two records for the 1777 southern-hemisphere chart and they have not been compared.
why_it_matters: The essay must name the copy it reproduces. Two records for one chart is the ambiguity the register exists to close.
next_action: Open rmgc-object-543571 and record whether it is a second impression, a different state or a duplicate cataloguing.

statement: No holding copy or plate state has been identified for the Fine, Mercator or Ortelius world maps.
why_it_matters: The southern coastline differs across states. A comparison of 'the Ortelius world map' with no state named compares nothing in particular.
next_action: Select one holding copy per object, record its identifier, and note the state on which the southern coast is read.

statement: No Bellingshausen chart has been located in a named repository.
why_it_matters: The 1820 priority discussion cannot be illustrated from the Russian side, which would leave the essay arguing priority from British and American material alone.
next_action: Identify the expedition atlas plates and a holding institution; establish whether a digitised set exists.

statement: The essay's access to Bellingshausen is through Debenham's 1945 English edition.
why_it_matters: Priority claims often turn on the wording of what was seen. A translation is an interpretation and may not silently stand in for the Russian text.
next_action: Either consult the Russian text for the passages the essay quotes, or declare the dependence on Debenham in the claim ledger and the essay.

statement: No specific Wilkes chart sheet or charted position has been identified.
why_it_matters: The programme's flagship ghost-geography case is currently a general recollection that Ross sailed over land Wilkes charted. Which land, at what position, on which sheet, is unknown.
next_action: Locate the United States Exploring Expedition atlas sheets and record the disputed positions with their coordinates.

statement: The Endurance22 site returned 403 and the Antarctic Treaty HSM 93 entry could not be retrieved.
why_it_matters: The Coda compares a 1915 reported position with a 2022 confirmed one. Neither figure is currently held from a citable source, and secondary reporting conflates the two.
next_action: Obtain the wreck position from the HSM 93 designation or a peer-reviewed publication, together with a stated uncertainty.

statement: Worsley's navigational records have not been located in a named archive.
why_it_matters: Without them the dataset cannot distinguish an observed fix from a dead-reckoned position, which is the whole subject of Act VIII.
next_action: Search the Scott Polar Research Institute and Royal Geographical Society catalogues for the Endurance navigational material.

statement: No reviewed table of dated Endurance positions has been compiled from a primary or scholarly source.
why_it_matters: A drift track drawn from a narrative is an illustration. The interactive claims to show recorded positions and must be able to cite each one.
next_action: Compile positions from Worsley and Shackleton with page locators, then mark which are observed and which are inferred.

statement: The Greenwich record dates the ice chart 1910 and 1874, and a separate 1874 record exists; the two sheets have not been compared.
why_it_matters: If the 1910 sheet revises an 1874 compilation, Act VII can show a synthesis being corrected rather than merely accumulating.
next_action: Open rmgc-object-555864 and establish the relationship between the two sheets.

statement: No scholarship has been consulted that attributes any specific southern ghost feature to mirage, refraction or ice.
why_it_matters: Attributing a cause to an error is a much stronger claim than recording that it was later removed, and the specification flags it as high risk.
next_action: Find peer-reviewed work on Antarctic refraction and ice-island misidentification before any causal statement is drafted.

statement: Headland's chronology has not been consulted, so no date in this programme has been checked against a reference work.
why_it_matters: Dates are the spine of Acts V to VIII and are the easiest thing to get quietly wrong.
next_action: Consult the chronology and record an entry against each dated record in the observations table.
